description: Add the /ste controlled-language writing standard for artifact prose, with a deterministic checker, and publish a portable copy to the mifunedev/skills registry.

userStories.title: Ship the checker script
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want a deterministic checker so that a compliance claim is testable instead of asserted.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh` exists and is executable.
The script sets `set -euo pipefail`.
The script resolves its own directory and reads no `CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR` variable.
The script accepts one or more file arguments and the flag `--blocks <tag>`.
Without `--blocks`, the script lints narrative prose and skips YAML frontmatter, fenced blocks, and HTML comments.
With `--blocks after`, the script lints only lines inside fenced blocks whose info string ends in `after`.
The script strips inline code spans, link targets, and bare URLs before it matches a pattern.
The script reports each finding as `file:line: RULE-ID message`.
The script exits 0 for clean input, 1 when it reports a finding, and 2 for a usage error.
The script writes to no file it was given.
`bash -n .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh` reports no syntax error.

The script detects all six classes: hedges and qualifiers, vague nouns and pronouns, passive-voice markers, sentences over the word cap, compound actions in one step, and non-approved words from the dictionary.
userStories.notes: Built first. US-001, US-003, and US-005 all assert against it.

userStories.title: Author the rules reference
userStories.description: As a documentation agent, I want a complete rule set so that I apply one standard instead of ad-hoc style judgement.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/ste/references/rules.md` exists.
`command grep -c '^### ' .oh/skills/ste/references/rules.md` reports 53.
`command grep -c '^## ' .oh/skills/ste/references/rules.md` reports 10, which is 9 rule sections plus `## Contents`.
Every rule heading carries a stable identifier of the form `### N. <title>`.
The file opens with a `## Contents` list because it is longer than 100 lines.
The file links to no other file under `references/`.
The file states no ASD-STE100 Issue 9 text and no ASD-STE100 dictionary entry.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .oh/skills/ste/references/rules.md` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004 for the self-check.

userStories.title: Author the dictionary reference
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a non-approved to approved word map so that terminology choices are deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/ste/references/dictionary.md` exists.
The file maps 150 or more non-approved words to approved replacements, one pipe-table row per entry.
Every word in both columns is wrapped in backticks so that the checker treats it as code.

The file states that the map is scoped to software documentation, that it is not the ASD-STE100 controlled dictionary, and that every entry was authored from software documentation practice rather than filtered from any published word list.
The file opens with a `## Contents` list.
The file links to no other file under `references/`.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .oh/skills/ste/references/dictionary.md` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004. The self-check passes only because the checker strips inline code spans.

userStories.title: Author the examples reference
userStories.description: As an agent that rewrites prose, I want before and after pairs so that I pattern-match the transformation.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/ste/references/examples.md` exists.
`command grep -c '^```text before$'` reports 20 or more, and the count of `after` fences equals the count of `before` fences.
Every pair carries a `**Domain:**` label and a `**Rules:**` label on the lines above it.

`command grep -o '^\*\*Domain:\*\* .*'` reports 13 or more distinct domain values covering CLI help, Docker, Linux administration, API documentation, configuration files, deployment, troubleshooting, warnings, prerequisites, Git, coding-agent instructions, architecture documents, and end-user documentation.
One pair shows a rewrite that is valid only when the source resolves the pronoun, and the pair states that condition.
One pair shows preserved ambiguity with a placeholder instead of an invented value.
The file opens with a `## Contents` list.
The file links to no other file under `references/`.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .oh/skills/ste/references/examples.md` exits 0.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh --blocks after .oh/skills/ste/references/examples.md` exits 0.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh --blocks before .oh/skills/ste/references/examples.md` exits 1 and reports a finding from every one of the six detector classes.
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004. The before blocks are the committed regression fixture for the checker.

userStories.title: Author SKILL.md
userStories.description: As an agent selecting a skill, I want one entry point that states the standard, the two modes, and the precedence rule.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/skills/ste/SKILL.md` exists and is shorter than 500 lines.
The frontmatter holds only the keys `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`, and `metadata`.
The description states the trigger conditions.
The body holds a line-anchored `## Memory Protocol` heading.
The body holds a line-anchored `## Reference` heading.
The body states that the skill claims no ASD-STE100 certification and no complete standards compliance.
The body states the precedence rule over `/caveman`.
The body states rewrite mode as a numbered procedure.
The body states authoring mode as a numbered procedure.
The body states the CONDITION, ACTOR, ACTION, OBJECT, EXPECTED RESULT sentence frame.
The body holds a 10-question sentence checklist.
The body states that a writer must not invent a missing value and must mark it with a placeholder instead.
The body states that code, commands, API names, filenames, paths, identifiers, configuration keys, and quoted literals are never simplified.
The body links `references/rules.md`, `references/dictionary.md`, `references/examples.md`, and `scripts/ste-check.sh` by exact relative path.
`bash .oh/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .oh/skills/ste/SKILL.md` exits 0.
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 through US-004 for exact filenames and checker behaviour.

userStories.title: Wire the skill into the harness
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the skill listed where I look for skills so that it is discoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: `AGENTS.md` holds one `/ste` row in the Skills table.
`CHANGELOG.md` holds one `### Added` line under `## [Unreleased]` that links issue 750.
No repository file outside `.oh/skills/ste/`, `.oh/tasks/ste-controlled-language/`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` changes.

userStories.title: Verify the change and record evidence
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want recorded evidence so that I do not re-run the whole suite to trust the claim.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/tasks/ste-controlled-language/verify.sh` runs every check and exits non-zero when any check fails.
Each checker assertion compares the exit code and fails the script on a mismatch, rather than printing the code.
`bash .oh/skills/eval/run.sh` reports no new regression against the 97-probe baseline captured before the change.
`git grep` for the legacy hyphenated reference tokens over `.oh/skills/ste` returns no match after staging.
Every file under `references/` longer than 100 lines opens with `## Contents`.
`git add -f .oh/tasks/ste-controlled-language/` stages the task folder, which `.gitignore:12` would otherwise exclude.
`.oh/tasks/ste-controlled-language/evidence.md` records observed commands and real output only.
`git diff --name-only upstream/development...HEAD` lists no path under `.oh/memory/` and no `.oh/evals/RESULTS.md`.

userStories.title: Publish the portable copy to the registry
userStories.description: As a user of another project, I want to install the skill from the public registry.
acceptanceCriteria: `skills/ste/` in `mifunedev/skills` holds `SKILL.md`, the three reference files, and the script.
The frontmatter holds only keys from the allow-list `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, `license`, `metadata`.
`skills/ste/LICENSE` holds the MIT text from the registry root.
`registry.json` holds one `ste` entry with all 11 required fields.
`npx --yes skills-ref@0.1.5 validate ./skills/ste/` passes.
`./scripts/refresh-checksums.sh` runs after the last content edit.
`./scripts/validate.sh` prints PASS.
userStories.notes: Must not start before US-007 passes. Any later content edit invalidates the checksum.

userStories.title: Open both pull requests and file the follow-up issue
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the change delivered and the deferred decision recorded so that neither is silently dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: A pull request on `mifunedev/openharness` targets `development` from `skill/750-ste-controlled-language`, titled `FROM skill/750-ste-controlled-language TO development`, with `Closes #750` in the body.
The harness pull request body links the evidence file and states the validation output.
A pull request on `mifunedev/skills` targets the registry default branch and holds the `validate.sh` output under a `## Testing` heading.
One follow-up issue records the council verdict on `/caveman` consolidation and names the licensing artifacts a removal would touch.
